= Architecture & Request Flow

This page explains how {mcp-gw} works under the hood - what each component does and how a request travels from an AI agent through the gateway to an MCP server and back.

TIP: All file paths and `oc apply` commands in this guide are relative to the link:{repo-url}[mcp-gateway-guide] repository root.

IMPORTANT: This guide is not a replacement for the link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_connectivity_link/1.4/html/install_the_mcp_gateway/mcp-gateway-install[official {rhcl} {mcp-gw} documentation].

== Component Overview

{mcp-gw} is built from three components, each with a distinct responsibility:

[cols="1,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Component | Role | Details

| *MCP Broker*
| Default backend at `/mcp`
| Handles `initialize` and `tools/list` requests. Connects to all configured MCP servers, discovers their tools, and returns an aggregated tool list with prefixes. Caches the tool list and brokers SSE notifications between clients and servers.

| *MCP Router*
| Envoy ext_proc filter
| Intercepts `tools/call` requests via Envoy external processing. Parses the tool name to determine the target server based on prefix, sets routing headers (`x-mcp-servername`, `x-mcp-toolname`, `:authority`), strips the prefix before forwarding, and manages backend MCP sessions.

| *MCP Gateway Controller*
| Kubernetes controller
| Watches `MCPServerRegistration` custom resources, resolves `HTTPRoute` references to backend URLs, generates a ConfigMap with the server configuration consumed by both the broker and router, and triggers reloads when the configuration changes.
|===

== Request Flow

Here is what happens when an AI agent interacts with the {mcp-gw}, from initialization through tool discovery and tool execution.

++++
<img src="https://mermaid." alt="MCP Gateway request flow" style="display:block;margin:0 auto;max-width:100%;" />
++++

_Diagram source: link:https://docs.kuadrant.io/dev/mcp-gateway/docs/design/overview/[Upstream MCP Gateway Design^]_

=== 1. Initialize Session

The client sends an `initialize` request to the gateway's `/mcp` endpoint. The Gateway routes it to the MCP Broker (default backend). The broker responds with server capabilities and the `mcp-session-id` header that the client must include in all subsequent requests.

[source,json]
----
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
 "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": {"name": "my-agent", "version": "1.0"}}}
----

=== 2. Discover Tools

The client sends a `tools/list` request with the session ID. The broker returns the aggregated list of tools from all registered MCP servers, each prefixed with the server's configured `toolPrefix`:

[source]
----
test1_greet, test1_headers, test1_time, ...   <-- from test-server1
risk_calculate_dti, risk_calculate_ltv, ...   <-- from risk-server
discover_tools, select_tools                  <-- built-in gateway tools
----

=== 3. Call a Tool

When the client sends a `tools/call` request (e.g., `test1_greet`), the request takes a different path:

1. The request arrives at the Gateway's public `mcp` listener
2. The Envoy **ext_proc** filter intercepts it and sends it to the MCP Router
3. The router parses the tool name, identifies `test1_` as the prefix for `test-server1`
4. The router sets the `:authority` header to the target server's hostname (e.g., `server1.mcp.local`) and strips the prefix from the tool name (`test1_greet` becomes `greet`)
5. The router also sets `x-mcp-servername` and `x-mcp-toolname` headers (used by authorization policies)
6. Envoy routes the request to the correct MCP server based on the `:authority` header via the internal `mcps` listener
7. The MCP server processes the tool call and returns the result

=== 4. Session Management

The router maintains two types of session mappings:

* *Client sessions* - Created by the broker during `initialize`. Maps the client to a gateway session ID.
* *Backend sessions* - Created lazily by the router on the first `tools/call` to each backend server. Maps `gateway-session-id/server-name` to a `backend-mcp-session-id`.

This means the router only initializes a backend MCP session when the client actually calls a tool from that server, not during the initial `tools/list` discovery.

=== 5. Response

The MCP server returns the tool result as an SSE response (`event: message\ndata: {...}`). The response flows back through the Gateway to the client.

== Envoy Filter Chain

When authentication and authorization are enabled (Phases 7-8), the Envoy filter chain processes requests in this order:

[cols="1,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Order | Filter | Purpose

| 1
| ext_proc (MCP Router)
| Parses MCP protocol, sets routing headers (`INSERT_FIRST`)

| 2
| WASM (Kuadrant)
| Evaluates AuthPolicy rules - JWT validation on `mcp` listener, CEL authorization on `mcps` listener (`INSERT_BEFORE ROUTER`)

| 3
| Router
| Routes to the target backend based on `:authority` header
|===

This ordering means the MCP Router sets `x-mcp-toolname` and `x-mcp-servername` headers *before* the Kuadrant WASM filter evaluates authorization policies. This is why tool-level authorization works on the internal `mcps` listener but not on the public `mcp` listener (see xref:08-authorization.adoc[Phase 8]).
